a: A hold is not released by `clock.ramp(...)`: the clock plays away from the held time while the hold stays live
`holdPosition` puts an ended integer-loop position in a pass that does not exist, so a changed origin lands it at the end instead of at the same shown time
`declare` re-derives the default `speed` from the clock's current rate instead of the declared rate, so re-declaring the same spec changes `speed`
`holdAt` and `holdPosition` give `pending()` two different answers for a time past the pass's end
A clock that a second registration under its id shadows stops being synced, and jumps forward by the whole shadowed time when it comes back
`reset()` throws on a clock opened at `start: 'end'` once a `declare` has made its run endless
b: `declare` defaults an omitted `speed` from the clock's current rate, so a paused clock redeclared loses its speed
`holdPosition` reads a finished run's position as the start of a pass that does not exist, while `declare` reads it as the end of the last pass
A ramp started from a paused, held clock does not release the hold, which keeps reporting `pending` and seeking it back
`setDuration` between endless and finite keeps a stale `edge`, where `applyRun` clears it
`reset()` throws on a clock declared `start: 'end'` once its loop is made endless
`holdAt.pending` compares a float round trip, not the elapsed it sought, so it can report a hold already met
